fixes.explanation: Father is close to home, but it's not the word. The LORD says, “…and the older will serve the younger.” That comes after He says one people will be stronger than the other, so the word you want is younger. Nobody's father is in that line.

No strangers in this verse, friend. The LORD says, “…the older will serve the younger.” That line comes after He says the two peoples will be separated and one will be stronger. Nobody new walks in, and the word is younger.

Good Bible name, but it's not this baby's. Reuben is Jacob's firstborn son (Genesis 35:23), so he comes after Jacob. The boy grasping Esau's heel is named Jacob. He's got his hands full right now, and none of them are holding a baby.

Not this time, friend. Jacob says, “Swear to me first…” so he wants an oath before anything changes hands. Esau gives it, and that's how the birthright gets sold. Jacob was not taking anybody's word for it, and I respect the hustle.
